tooley.q: A bus that supports the transfer of data in both directions is referred to as:
tooley.explain: A bus that can carry data both ways is called bidirectional (e.g. ARINC 629, AFDX, MIL-STD-1553); ARINC 429 by contrast is unidirectional only.

tooley.q: The main advantage of using a serial bus in an aircraft is:
opts: reduction in the size and weight of cabling
it supports the highest possible data rates
there is no need for data conversion
tooley.explain: A serial bus needs only one or two wire pairs instead of dozens of parallel wires, sharply cutting weight and installation space, matching reason #1 in the lecture slide (fewer wires, lower weight).

tooley.q: Which one of the following is used to minimise reflections present in a bus cable:
tooley.explain: A terminating resistor (e.g. 78Ω at both ends of the ARINC 629 bus, per the lecture slide) absorbs the signal at the end of the cable, preventing reflections that would otherwise cause interference.

tooley.q: The data format in an ARINC 429 stub cable consists of:
opts: parallel data from the local bus
tooley.explain: Per Tooley's own answer key, the ARINC 429 stub cable carries "serial analogue doublets": successive pairs of analogue voltage pulses, NOT Manchester-encoded data (easy to confuse, since Manchester is the encoding used by a different bus standard, ARINC 708/573).

tooley.q: In order to represent negative data values, BNR data uses:
opts: BCD data and a binary sign bit
an extra parity bit to indicate the sign
tooley.explain: BNR (Binary Number Representation) encodes a signed integer using two's complement across the 19-bit Data field, with bit 29 (the Data field's MSB) acting as the sign bit.

tooley.q: The physical bus media specified in ARINC 629 is:
tooley.explain: ARINC 629 uses shielded twisted pair (STP) cable, physically similar to ARINC 429, but with a very different protocol (2 Mbps, bidirectional, no central bus controller needed).

tooley.q: The validity of an ARINC 429 data word is checked by using:
tooley.explain: The last bit (bit 32) of the 32-bit word is an odd-parity bit: the total count of 1-bits across the whole word is always odd, letting the receiver detect simple single-bit errors.

tooley.q: The label field in an ARINC 429 data word consists of:
tooley.explain: The Label occupies exactly 8 bits (bits 1-8), enough to encode 256 different data types (0-255), e.g. Label 203 = airspeed in the lecture's example label table.

tooley.q: The voltages present on an ARINC 429 data bus cable are:
tooley.explain: Each conductor (A or B) carries +5V, 0V or -5V with respect to ground; only the DIFFERENTIAL voltage between the two wires reaches ±10V. The question asks about the voltage ON THE CABLE (each wire), so the answer is ±5V.

tooley.q: The maximum bit rate supported by ARINC 429 is:
tooley.explain: ARINC 429 has two speeds: low speed 12.5 kbps (most common) and high speed 100 kbps, which is the MAXIMUM rate supported.

tooley.q: An ARINC 429 NULL state is represented by:
tooley.explain: NULL (no data present) corresponds to both wires A and B sitting at 0V, distinct from bit 1 (A=+5V, B=-5V) and bit 0 (A=-5V, B=+5V).

tooley.q: The maximum data rate supported by MIL-STD-1553 is:
tooley.explain: MIL-STD-1553B supports 1 Mbps, faster than ARINC 429 (max 100 kbps) but slower than ARINC 629 (2 Mbps) and AFDX (100 Mbps).

tooley.q: A bus that is self-clocking is referred to as:
tooley.explain: ARINC 429's BPRZ encoding always has a transition in the middle of every bit (return to 0V), so the receiver can recover timing from the signal itself with no separate clock wire: this is the self-clocking property.

tooley.q: The physical bus media specified in MIL-STD-1773B is:
tooley.explain: MIL-STD-1773B is the fibre-optic implementation of MIL-STD-1553B, giving much greater immunity to high-intensity radiated electromagnetic fields (HIRF) than copper cable.

tooley.q: The length of an ARINC 429 word is:
tooley.explain: An ARINC 429 word is always 32 bits long: Label(8)+SDI(2)+Data(19)+SSM(2)+Parity(1) = 32.

tooley.q: ARINC 573 is designed for use with:
tooley.explain: ARINC 573 is the standard for Flight Data Recorders (FDR), using 12-bit Harvard Bi-Phase encoding; ARINC 717 later superseded ARINC 573.

tooley.q: The maximum data rate supported by the FDDI bus is:
tooley.explain: FDDI (Fibre Distributed Data Interface), developed by Boeing for the 777, supports 100 Mbps over a dual token-ring topology.

generated.q: ARINC 629 supports a data transmission rate of:
generated.explain: ARINC 629 reaches 2 Mbps, 20 times faster than ARINC 429's top speed (100 kbps), matching the figures in the lecture slide.

generated.q: The channel access mechanism used by ARINC 629 is:
generated.explain: ARINC 629 uses TDMA: each LRU is assigned one or more fixed time slots within a Major Frame to transmit, avoiding data collisions without needing a central bus controller.

generated.q: AFDX (ARINC 664) achieves a maximum transmission rate of:
generated.explain: AFDX is 100 Mbps switched full-duplex Ethernet, using the Virtual Link (VL) mechanism to guarantee deterministic bandwidth for each data flow.

generated.q: In AFDX, the mechanism that guarantees each data flow its own bandwidth, preventing other flows from consuming it, is called:
generated.explain: Each Virtual Link has its own bandwidth, frame size and transmission period (BAG); the AFDX switch isolates VLs from each other so that one faulty flow cannot congest the whole network.

generated.q: A central bus controller is a required component of which of the following bus standards?
generated.explain: MIL-STD-1553B uses a command-response architecture with one Bus Controller (BC) managing up to 31 Remote Terminals (RT); ARINC 629, by contrast, was designed to need NO central bus controller (avoiding a single point of failure).

generated.q: The SSM field in an ARINC 429 data word is used to:
opts: specify which device receives the data
report data status (valid, failure, test mode...)
identify the type of data being transmitted
generated.explain: SSM (Sign/Status Matrix, 2 bits) reports one of 4 context-dependent data states, e.g. for BNR: 00=Failure Warning, 01=No Computed Data, 10=Functional Test, 11=Normal Operation.

generated.q: If a 32-bit ARINC 429 word is transmitted at 100 kbps, the time to transmit one word is:
generated.explain: t = N/R = 32 bits / 100,000 bit/s = 0.00032 s = 0.32 ms, matching the Data Rate and Bit Timing table in the lecture slide.
